cases.contract_context: Section 12.4 Governing Law and Jurisdiction: This Agreement and any disputes arising out of or related hereto shall be governed exclusively by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the State of Delaware, without giving effect to any choice or conflict of law provision or rule. Each party irrevocably consents to the exclusive personal jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New Castle County, Delaware.
cases.query: What is the governing law and jurisdiction specified in the NDA?
cases.model_answer: This agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, and all disputes must be brought before courts in Manhattan.
cases.human_rationale: Direct contradiction of Section 12.4. The contract designates Delaware and New Castle County, whereas the model hallucinated New York / Manhattan.

cases.contract_context:
[SUPERSEDED Draft 2023]: In the event of breach, Provider liability is capped at $5,000,000. 
[EXECUTED 2026 RESTATEMENT Clause 8.2]: Section 8.2 Total aggregate liability of Provider arising under or related to this Agreement shall in no event exceed the total fees paid by Customer during the twelve (12) months preceding the incident giving rise to liability.

cases.model_answer: Under the agreement terms, Provider liability is capped at $5,000,000 for any breach of contract.

cases.contract_context: Section 4.1 Payment Terms: Invoices are issued monthly on the first business day. Customer shall pay all undisputed invoices within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. Late payments shall accrue interest at the rate of 1.5% per month or the maximum rate permitted by law.

cases.model_answer: Customer must pay undisputed invoices within thirty (30) days of invoice receipt. Late payments accrue interest at 1.5% per month.
cases.human_rationale: Accurately represents both the 30-day payment term and 1.5% monthly late interest rate per Section 4.1.

cases.contract_context: Clause 14.2 Termination for Convenience: Either party may terminate this Agreement without cause upon providing at least ninety (90) days prior written notice to the other party, provided that Customer remains liable for all prepaid, non-refundable subscription fees.
cases.query: Can Customer terminate for convenience and get a refund on prepaid fees?
cases.model_answer: Yes, Customer may terminate without cause upon 90 days notice and will receive a full prorated refund for all unused prepaid subscription fees.
cases.human_rationale: Dangerous legal error. Clause 14.2 explicitly stipulates that prepaid fees are non-refundable, directly contradicted by the answer.

cases.contract_context: Section 1.1 Definitions: 'Personal Data Breach' means a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure of, or access to Customer Personal Data transmitted, stored or otherwise processed by Vendor.
cases.query: How is a security incident involving customer personal data defined?
cases.model_answer: Under Section 1.1, a 'Personal Data Breach' is defined as a security breach resulting in accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure of, or access to Customer Personal Data.
cases.human_rationale: Correctly references Section 1.1 and quotes the precise definition of Personal Data Breach.

cases.contract_context: Section 5 Deliverables and Acceptance: Customer shall have ten (10) business days following receipt of each Deliverable to inspect and accept or reject such Deliverable in writing.
cases.query: Is Vendor liable for consequential damages if milestone 3 is delayed?
cases.model_answer: Yes, Vendor is automatically subject to liquidated damages of $1,000 per calendar day for any delay in milestone 3.
cases.human_rationale: The SOW context contains no liquidated damages clause. The model fabricated a $1,000/day penalty out of thin air.

cases.contract_context: Clause 9.1 Indemnification: Provider shall defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from Provider's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or infringement of intellectual property rights. Provider's total liability under this Clause 9.1 is not subject to the limitation of liability in Section 8.
cases.query: Is IP infringement indemnification capped under the general limitation of liability in Section 8?
cases.model_answer: No, under Clause 9.1, IP infringement indemnification claims are expressly uncapped and exempt from the Section 8 liability ceiling.
cases.human_rationale: Legally accurate interpretation of the carve-out in Clause 9.1.

cases.contract_context: Section 3 Confidentiality Obligations: The Receiving Party shall protect Disclosing Party's Confidential Information with the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential information of like nature, but in no event less than a reasonable degree of care. These obligations shall survive for a period of three (3) years from the Effective Date.
cases.query: What is the required standard of care and survival period for confidential information?
cases.model_answer: The Receiving Party must use a strict fiduciary standard of utmost good faith, and obligations survive in perpetuity forever.
cases.human_rationale: Model substituted 'reasonable standard of care' with 'strict fiduciary standard' and 3-year term with 'perpetuity'.

cases.contract_context: Section 6.2 Work Product: Consultant agrees that all Deliverables and Work Product created under this Agreement shall be deemed 'work made for hire' owned exclusively by Client upon creation. If any Work Product does not qualify as work made for hire, Consultant hereby irrevocably assigns all right, title, and interest to Client.
cases.query: Who owns intellectual property developed by Consultant during the engagement?
cases.model_answer: All Work Product and Deliverables are owned exclusively by Client from creation as work made for hire, with an irrevocable assignment fallback under Section 6.2.
cases.human_rationale: Exact match to legal assignment mechanics in Section 6.2.

cases.contract_context: Section 2.1 Grant of License: Subject to the terms of this Agreement, Licensor grants Distributor a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to market and distribute the Software solely in the Territory (defined in Exhibit A as North America).
cases.query: Can Distributor grant sublicenses to European partners?
cases.model_answer: Yes, Distributor has full worldwide exclusive rights to sublicense the Software across Europe and Asia under Section 2.1.
cases.human_rationale: Direct violation of Section 2.1: license is non-exclusive, non-transferable, and restricted solely to North America.

cases.contract_context: Clause 4 Non-Solicitation of Employees: During employment and for twelve (12) months following termination, Employee shall not directly or indirectly solicit or recruit any current employee of Company to leave their employment.
cases.query: What is the duration of the non-solicitation restriction for employees?
cases.model_answer: The non-solicitation obligation applies during employment and continues for twelve (12) months after termination pursuant to Clause 4.
cases.human_rationale: Directly quotes and adheres to the 12-month post-termination covenant in Clause 4.

cases.contract_context: Section 3.2 Service Level Credits: If Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 99.9% but is at least 99.0%, Customer shall receive a 10% service credit. If uptime falls below 99.0%, Customer receives a 25% credit. Claims must be submitted within thirty (30) days of month end.
cases.query: What service credit is owed if availability is 99.4%, and how is it claimed?
cases.model_answer: If availability is 99.4%, Customer is entitled to a 10% service credit under Section 3.2, which must be claimed in writing within thirty (30) days of month end.
cases.human_rationale: Properly mapped 99.4% to the 99.0%-99.9% tier (10% credit) and included the 30-day claim deadline.

cases.contract_context: Section 8 Maintenance and Repairs: Tenant shall at its sole expense maintain the interior of the Leased Premises. Landlord shall be responsible for structural elements, roof, foundations, and exterior walls, provided Tenant provides prompt written notice of defects.
cases.query: Is Tenant responsible for roof replacement and structural foundation repairs?
cases.model_answer: Yes, Section 8 specifies that Tenant bears sole financial responsibility for all structural foundation and roof maintenance.
cases.human_rationale: Reversed the obligation. Section 8 explicitly places structural elements and roof on Landlord, not Tenant.

cases.contract_context: Section 11.1 Survival of Representations: Fundamental representations (Title, Organization, Authority) shall survive closing indefinitely. All other representations and warranties of Seller shall survive for eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date.
cases.query: How long do standard operational representations survive after closing?
cases.model_answer: All representations without exception expire immediately upon closing and cannot be sued upon.
cases.human_rationale: Contradicts Section 11.1: General representations survive for 18 months, and fundamental reps survive indefinitely.

cases.contract_context: Section 7 Insurance Requirements: Subcontractor shall maintain Commercial General Liability insurance with limits of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and $4,000,000 aggregate, naming Contractor as an Additional Insured.

cases.contract_context: Section 10 Audit Rights: Upon thirty (30) days advance written notice, Company may inspect Reseller's relevant sales records during normal business hours once per calendar year.

cases.model_answer: Yes, Company reserves the right to conduct surprise, unannounced physical audits 24/7 without notice.
cases.human_rationale: Contradicts Section 10 notice requirement (30 days advance written notice during business hours, max once per year).

cases.contract_context: Section 5.3 Severance Benefits: Upon termination without Cause or resignation for Good Reason, Executive is entitled to twelve (12) months base salary continuation and twelve (12) months COBRA premium reimbursement, contingent on signing a general release of claims.

cases.model_answer: If terminated for Cause, Executive is not entitled to salary continuation or COBRA severance under Section 5.3 (severance requires termination without Cause or Good Reason resignation).
cases.human_rationale: Correctly reasons from the conditional trigger in Section 5.3 that termination for Cause forfeits severance benefits.

cases.contract_context: Section 4.3 Background IP: Each party shall retain sole ownership of all Background Intellectual Property owned or controlled by such party prior to the Effective Date or developed independently outside the Scope of Work.

cases.model_answer: No, each party retains sole ownership of its Background IP developed prior to the Effective Date or independently outside the project per Section 4.3.
cases.human_rationale: Clear and faithful restatement of Background IP preservation in Section 4.3.
